findings.title: First signup deletes valid incoming email-link requests
findings.case: A adds offline B and sends an email request; B then creates an account.
findings.intended: B sees the pending request and can accept it.
findings.actual: Both legacy and current resumable signup cleanup delete the incoming request. B finishes signup with no request; A must resend.
findings.fix: Distinguish fresh incoming invitations from deleted-account artifacts. Preserve valid pending requests bound to an active sender and owned target.
findings.evidence: Two new expected-correct tests fail: expected one incoming request, received zero. Independently reproduced.

findings.title: Hydration treats another person with your name as you
findings.case: Two distinct Alex Smiths share a group; the other Alex paid dinner.
findings.intended: Keep both UUIDs, original payer, and settlement amounts.
findings.actual: normalizeGroup removes the other Alex solely by name; normalizeExpenses rewrites payer/splits to self. Dirty data is sent back to the backend. Mixed settlement states can also collapse.
findings.fix: Use trusted canonical/alias equivalence for identity. Separate historical name-based repair from normal hydration.
findings.evidence: Actual loadRemoteData XCTest fails: the other person disappears, payer changes, 3 shares become 2, settled self share becomes 60 unpaid instead of 30 settled. Independently traced.

findings.title: Merging duplicates can revive paid debt
findings.case: The same expense has B-old: $10 settled and B-new: $15 unpaid; A merges the people.
findings.intended: Keep $15 outstanding and $10 settled.
findings.actual: Amounts are summed and settlement flags ANDed: the result is $25 unpaid. Backend and iOS use this aggregation.
findings.fix: Preserve settled and outstanding portions. Until supported, reject mixed-state coalescence atomically. Changing AND to OR would instead forgive unpaid debt.
findings.evidence: Authenticated merge regression fails: expected 15, actual 25. Independent financial reviewer reran it.

findings.title: Legacy canonical bootstrap can claim a stranger’s placeholder
findings.case: An existing authenticated legacy account has no member_id and knows an unregistered person’s member ID.
findings.intended: Assign its own canonical identity; claiming someone else’s history requires consent-bound linking.
findings.actual: users.updateLinkedMemberId accepts that placeholder without owner/invite approval. A previously inaccessible private group and its expenses become readable. New accounts already receive random canonical IDs and cannot use this path.
findings.fix: Generate missing canonical IDs server-side. Route historical claims through the authenticated linking core. Audit legacy accounts without member_id read-only before any repair.
findings.evidence: Authenticated before/after group and expense reads reproduced and independently checked. Production prevalence of the legacy prerequisite is unknown.

findings.title: Successful linking can leave shared history absent from current sync
findings.case: A knows offline B; A/B/C share a group and C owns an expense involving B. B links through A.
findings.intended: B gains the relevant group/expense history after successful consent.
findings.actual: The alias installs, but V2 group and expense visibility remain empty for mixed-owner or C-owned history. Legacy alias-aware queries can see the group. Current iOS uses V2.
findings.fix: Reconcile derived visibility for every record affected by a trusted alias. Preserve foreign financial content and use bounded resumable indexing.
findings.evidence: Four expected-correct tests fail: invite and email acceptance, each with inviter-owned and third-party-owned groups. Explicit reconciliation makes the histories appear.

findings.title: Normal adjustments can persist negative or nonconserved debt
findings.case: A $20 expense starts with $10/$10; the user subtracts $15 from the friend’s adjustment.
findings.intended: Reject or rebalance the adjustment so valid shares conserve the expense total.
findings.actual: The saved shares are $10 and −$5, totaling $5. Backend also accepts NaN totals and Infinity shares from malformed clients.
findings.fix: Validate finite values, sign/refund policy, precision and conservation server-side; apply the same rules in the real UI splitting code.
findings.evidence: Authenticated payload tests persist negative/nonconserved and nonfinite amounts. UI adjustment and save paths traced independently.

findings.title: Selected currency is discarded
findings.case: Enter 100 EUR, then view the expense on a US-locale device.
findings.intended: Preserve denomination and value; balances must use an explicit currency contract.
findings.actual: Currency changes the form’s presentation, but Expense, DTO and schema store no currency and no conversion occurs. Detail views label 100 with the viewer’s locale, e.g. $100.
findings.fix: Temporarily constrain to one explicit currency or introduce a complete currency-aware storage, display and balance contract. Existing historical denomination cannot be inferred reliably.
findings.evidence: Reachable picker → save → model → backend → detail cross-layer source trace; not simulator-verified.

findings.title: Recovery can publish A’s friends into B’s local state
findings.case: Recovery starts for A, friend fetch suspends, then B signs in before completion.
findings.intended: Discard every completion from A.
findings.actual: reconcileAfterNetworkRecovery invokes reconciliation without a context; stale-result checks are conditional. A’s remote friends can be merged with B’s current list.
findings.fix: Require account ID and data epoch for every reconciliation; check after each await and before state publication.
findings.evidence: Deterministic suspend/switch/resume XCTest fails: A’s friend remains in B’s friend set. Reachable network/app-activation callers traced.

findings.title: Friend-sync batches are not bound to the starting account
findings.case: A multirow friend sync suspends; the shared Convex authentication changes to B.
findings.intended: Stop or reject A’s remaining writes.
findings.actual: The real adapter ignores accountEmail and sends separately awaited upserts without per-write session/cancellation checks. Later rows may execute as B. Mocks partition by accountEmail and hide this risk.
findings.fix: Validate expected actor on each server write and cancellation/session generation between batch operations. Apply the same discipline to chunked import.
findings.evidence: Cross-layer code trace; live auth-switch reproduction not performed. This is a supported race risk, not a demonstrated production incident.

findings.title: Import silently merges different people with equal names
findings.case: An export contains two different Bobs with distinct UUIDs, even into an empty account.
findings.intended: Preserve each source identity unless the user explicitly merges it.
findings.actual: Name-keyed mapping collapses two friends into one and creates duplicate member IDs within a group. This also occurs with createNew.
findings.fix: Preserve source UUID mapping independently. Use names only to suggest an explicit user choice.
findings.evidence: Actual model/export/parser/import harness: 2 friends → 1; 3 member rows → 2 unique IDs. Independently rerun.

findings.title: Backups drop grouped-individual expenses
findings.case: Export a multi-friend expense created without a persisted group, then restore.
findings.intended: Restore context, participants, splits, settlement and notes.
findings.actual: Export omits contextKind. iOS import skips an expense without a mapped group; backend import also requires a group reference. One exported expense becomes zero imported. Notes are omitted for ordinary expenses too.
findings.fix: Version the backup contract, include context and notes, and support group-free import without fabricating a group.
findings.evidence: Actual production import/export source harness reproduces loss; adapter replaces network/storage, so this is not a complete live backend transaction.

findings.title: Multiline CSV fields lose expenses on restore
findings.case: An expense description contains a newline.
findings.intended: Round-trip the quoted multiline field.
findings.actual: Exporter quotes it, but importer splits physical lines before CSV parsing; the expense fragments are silently skipped.
findings.fix: Parse logical CSV records across quoted newlines and surface malformed-row errors.
findings.evidence: Actual exporter/parser harness: one exported expense → zero parsed expenses.

findings.title: Import turns group participants into local confirmed friends
findings.case: Restore a group containing someone absent from the explicit friend list.
findings.intended: Keep the person in group history only.
findings.actual: Importer appends every non-self group member to local friends with confirmed status. Production bulk import sends only explicit friend rows, causing local/server disagreement; the alternate CI path syncs the promoted list.
findings.fix: Import friendship only from explicit friend records and preserve group participants separately.
findings.evidence: Actual import transformation harness: zero exported friends → one local confirmed friend.

findings.title: An active invite cannot be resent through the app
findings.case: Create an invite, dismiss its share sheet or lose the URL, then tap Send Invite Link.
findings.intended: Reuse the active invite or deliberately revoke and replace it.
findings.actual: Client generates a new UUID; backend rejects another active token for the friend. Existing list/revoke APIs have no UI callers. The default active lifetime is 30 days.
findings.fix: Return/reuse the existing active token and construct the URL from the returned ID. Offer an explicit replacement path.
findings.evidence: Existing abuse-control test proves backend rejection; actual iOS callers traced.

findings.title: Stale Decline/Cancel can change accepted linking history
findings.case: One device accepts a request; another declines it or the sender cancels it afterward.
findings.intended: Reject terminal-state actions and preserve acceptance evidence.
findings.actual: Decline changes accepted to declined; cancel deletes the accepted request. New marked links remain linked with inconsistent history; legacy links depending on historical evidence become visibly unlinked.
findings.fix: Require pending state and retain durable acceptance provenance. Test stale actions and immutable accepted history.
findings.evidence: Four expected-correct failures, including visible legacy linked state true → false.

findings.title: Normal accumulated history can permanently block linking or merging
findings.case: A relevant friendship has 65 expenses, or a duplicate merge touches one 12-person expense.
findings.intended: Complete through safe bounded continuation.
findings.actual: More than 64 relevant expenses reject. A fixed 80-lookups-per-ID estimate rejects 13 priced IDs at 1,040 > 1,024 even without aliases. Retrying cannot reduce history; no continuation exists.
findings.fix: Budget actual indexed work and design resumable identity/reference/visibility reconciliation with appropriate fences. Raising constants alone is insufficient.
findings.evidence: Existing 64/65 boundary tests pass their rejection contract; new expected-success 12-person regression fails.

findings.title: Cleared shared expenses can return after someone else updates them
findings.case: B clears expenses, groups and friends; A later settles an old shared expense.
findings.intended: B remains detached while A’s history is preserved.
findings.actual: Clear-all removes derived visibility but not a durable exclusion. Later reconciliation recreates B’s visibility and the old expense reappears.
findings.fix: Persist per-account suppression/revocation and honor it on all visibility reconstruction paths.
findings.evidence: Authenticated complete Clear All sequence followed by another participant’s settlement reproduces reappearance.

findings.title: Stale linked-friend deletion becomes false local success
findings.case: B deletes their account; A still has linked B cached and deletes that friend.
findings.intended: Delete current server state or report failure and restore local state.
findings.actual: Backend returns success:false for ghost/unlinked state. iOS discards the result, retains its deletion tombstone and hides a server row that still exists until reset.
findings.fix: Enforce the response or throw on failure; preferably let one server operation handle the current relationship state atomically.
findings.evidence: Backend contract reproduced; adapter/tombstone path independently traced by iOS reviewer.

findings.title: 513 unrelated owned expenses block deleting an unused friend
findings.case: A has 513 owned expenses and deletes a friend with no history.
findings.intended: Complete friend deletion safely.
findings.actual: Cleanup collects all owned expenses before targeting the person and rejects beyond 512. No resumable user path exists.
findings.fix: Use indexed target references and/or durable bounded deletion jobs.
findings.evidence: Authenticated reproduction passes by asserting the safety-limit error and preserved friend.

findings.title: Stale devices create duplicate direct ledgers
findings.case: Two devices independently save first direct expenses for the same pair using different draft UUIDs.
findings.intended: Reuse one identity-equivalent server ledger.
findings.actual: Backend only looks up the supplied UUID and inserts a second container. Distinct expense IDs remain distinct; this alone does not double-count debt in the friend balance.
findings.fix: Resolve a canonical pair transactionally and return the chosen ledger identity to each client.
findings.evidence: Two sequential authenticated saves reproduce two direct groups; no timing race required.

findings.title: Existing ledgers and ordinary groups allow inconsistent financial participants
findings.case: An A/B ledger declares A/B involved but names unrelated C as payer or split participant; ordinary group payload names C outside the group.
findings.intended: Payer, splits and participant records must agree with the authorized identity set.
findings.actual: Both payload classes persist; unrelated registered C receives visibility to the fabricated new expense. New-direct/grouped-individual paths have stronger matching-set checks than these paths.
findings.fix: Apply canonical participant-set and payer validation to every write/context, with narrow historical compatibility.
findings.evidence: Two authenticated reproduction tests. Scope is injection/sharing of a newly created expense, not proof of reading C’s existing history.

findings.title: Unproven linked email grants visibility to a newly created expense
findings.case: Submit an offline friend B with C’s registered email as linked participant metadata.
findings.intended: Derive registered recipients only from trusted member/link provenance.
findings.actual: C can read the new expense through the authenticated expense list even though B is unlinked. This shares/injects creator data into C’s account.
findings.fix: Reject inconsistent linkage and stop treating input-derived email as independent visibility authority.
findings.evidence: Authenticated create and C read reproduced. Does not establish access to C’s unrelated data.

findings.title: Two add-friend paths confirm people before persistence succeeds
findings.case: Email Add’s first friend write fails, or a group-only detail Add Friend runs offline.
findings.intended: Confirm and show success only after remote friend persistence.
findings.actual: Email flow appends before sync and keeps the row after failure. Group-person detail uses addImportedFriend and immediately emits success. Normal Add Friend correctly awaits persistence.
findings.fix: Route these flows through the acknowledged add operation; keep confirmation only after the friend write succeeds.
findings.evidence: Email persistence failure XCTest fails: confirmedFriends is nonempty after the first friend write fails. Detail-view path source traced.

findings.title: Adding by name can choose the wrong historical person
findings.case: Work Alex and School Alex have different UUIDs; user adds a friend named Alex.
findings.intended: Preserve ambiguity and require selection, or create a distinct identity.
findings.actual: knownGroupParticipants first collapses UUIDs by name, so manualFriendCandidate sees an apparently unique person and reuses an arbitrary historical UUID.
findings.fix: Count distinct identity-equivalent candidates before display-name projection; never infer uniqueness after name deduplication.
findings.evidence: Deterministic same-name XCTest fails: candidate reuses one of the two unrelated historical UUIDs.

findings.title: Release builds still use Clerk development authentication
findings.case: Archive the Release app that targets production Convex.
findings.intended: Use coordinated production authentication and backend configuration.
findings.actual: AppConfig has one pk_test_ key for all configurations; backend trusts the corresponding accounts.dev issuer. Clerk documents a 100-user development cap and says development instances are unsuitable for production.
findings.fix: Configure auth by environment and plan account-ID continuity deliberately. A blind key switch can strand existing users.
findings.evidence: Repository configuration plus current official Clerk environment/deployment documentation. Actual dashboard configuration and deployed state were not inspected.

findings.title: Repeating the legacy friend request downgrades its status
findings.case: A and B already accepted a legacy friend request; A sends again.
findings.intended: Keep confirmed status and return an idempotent result.
findings.actual: The confirmed row becomes request_sent while linked flags remain true. Current direct-expense eligibility survives. No active UI caller was found.
findings.fix: Preserve confirmed rows in the legacy send path.
findings.evidence: New expected-correct test fails; linked flags and impact checked.

findings.title: One-way email acceptance leaves an existing manual inviter without a merge path
findings.case: B already tracks A manually with expenses; A sends B an email request and B accepts.
findings.intended: Offer an explicit choice to merge B’s existing A record into linked A, preserving history. Do not guess from a name.
findings.actual: B has the old manual A plus new linked canonical A. Email acceptance has no merge selection; Settings merge allows only two unlinked friends, so that UI cannot repair this pair afterward. Crossed requests or invite claim with selection behave differently.
findings.fix: Add an owner-validated optional local merge selection to email acceptance, using the same atomic semantics as invite claim.
findings.evidence: Authenticated API characterization returns both visible rows; client merge eligibility and email accept view traced.

findings.title: Direct expense permissions are asymmetric after removing friendship
findings.case: A/B accept a request and A creates a ledger. B clears friends and submits a new direct expense; separately A clears friends and edits notes on retained history.
findings.intended: Require confirmed friendship for new exposure; allow authorized owner edits to unchanged historical participants.
findings.actual: B can still create because A’s persisted is_current_user flag bypasses A’s friendship check. Conversely, A’s notes-only update is rejected after A removes friendship.
findings.fix: Derive self only from authenticated identity. Separate new participant exposure from owner edits to retained historical records.
findings.evidence: Both cases reproduced through actual public request acceptance and friend removal. Normal picker hides removed friend; stale/API writes remain possible.

findings.title: Rounding tests do not exercise production equal splitting
findings.case: Split $10 equally among three people.
findings.intended: Allocate minor units deterministically, e.g. $3.34/$3.33/$3.33.
findings.actual: Production stores three repeating Double fractions, displayed as $3.33 each. Existing rounding tests call a separate test-only helper that allocates cents correctly.
findings.fix: Move minor-unit splitting into production and test that exact implementation across split modes/currency precision.
findings.evidence: Production call path and test helper compared; source evidence, not a simulator assertion.
